turns.content: Use Earth as the density reference for four planets: an Earth-mass/Earth-radius planet; a two-Earth-mass planet with density 5.5 g/cm^3; and Earth-composition rocky planets of five and one-half Earth mass.
Compare the first two planets quantitatively with Earth's mean density.
For the two Earth-composition planets, use the rocky-planet mass-radius trend to explain how self-compression changes mean density as mass increases.
Combine the stated density and self-compression comparisons to rank the four planets and identify the densest by physical description.
Check that the ranking does not assume radius proportional to mass, and distinguish equal composition from equal mean density.
State which planet has the highest mean density and why.
